title: Majestic Geniality
summary: Underpromote to avoid stalemate, then use the king to turn the rook blockade into mate.

nodes.question: Which promotion keeps a forced win?
nodes.explanation: After ...Rxd5, White has Kb8, h7 and b4 against Ka6, Rd5 and b5. Queen promotion creates a stalemate trap; a rook deliberately leaves more space.

branches.title: Underpromote and improve the king
commentary: Begin after ...Rxd5 in the stable six-piece final phase. The earlier ten-piece bishop/rook sacrifices remain context.
h8=R avoids the queen’s extra diagonal control and threatens Rh6 mate.
Rd6 blocks the sixth rank and stops that immediate mating idea.
Kc7 attacks Rd6 and controls b6. It also clears the eighth-rank route for Ra8 mate.
Rg6 is the source’s selected rook retreat. It still blocks the sixth rank, but cannot prevent the new Ra8 mating threat.
Ra8# is actual mate. Kc7 covers b6 and b7, b4 controls a5 and Black’s b5 pawn blocks the remaining flight.
branches.explanation: Ra8# is actual mate. Kc7 covers b6 and b7, b4 controls a5 and Black’s b5 pawn blocks the remaining flight.

branches.title: Promote to a queen and accept the rook
commentary: Compare the source’s natural queen promotion.
h8=Q gives up the forced win by allowing a rook sacrifice that uses the queen’s diagonal control.
Rd8+ offers the rook with check along the eighth rank.
Qxd8 is actual stalemate. Qd8 covers a5 and b6, Kb8 covers a7 and b7, and Black’s b5 pawn is blocked by b4. Ka6 is not in check.
branches.explanation: Qxd8 is actual stalemate. Qd8 covers a5 and b6, Kb8 covers a7 and b7, and Black’s b5 pawn is blocked by b4. Ka6 is not in check.

branches.title: Test the same sacrifice against a rook
commentary: This independent representative line tests why the queen’s stalemate defense does not work after rook promotion.
h8=R keeps White’s exact win and leaves diagonal flight squares available.
Rd8+ offers the same checking rook sacrifice.
Rxd8 captures the rook. Unlike Qxd8, it does not control b6 diagonally.
Kb6 is legal, so there is no stalemate. White retains an exactly checked rook-and-pawn win.
branches.classification: independent alternative with representative legal replies
branches.explanation: Kb6 is legal, so there is no stalemate. White retains an exactly checked rook-and-pawn win.

exercises.prompt: Why is a rook better than a queen here?
exercises.answer: After ...Rd8+ Qxd8 the queen covers b6 and a5, stalemating Ka6. A rook on d8 leaves b6 available, so capturing does not stalemate Black.

exercises.prompt: Why does Kc7 change the mating threat?
exercises.answer: It attacks the blockading rook and controls b6 and b7, letting Ra8 close the a-file once the rook moves away.

startContext: Begin after ...Rxd5 at 90 seconds in the visually reconstructed six-piece final phase. The earlier ten-piece setup and intermediate bishop/rook ideas are source context. Rook promotion, the selected ...Rd6/...Rg6 mating line and queen stalemate are checked; the parallel rook-capture escape is independently supplied.
